concepts.label: Application-authored retry decorator (allow_retries, fixed/linear/exponential backoff)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - REJECTED reuse of sdk:retry-strategy after checking the page. Java's extraction-layer sdk:retry-strategy is described as an SDK-BUILT-IN, transparent 'pre-exception decision layer' (RetryStrategy/RetryReason) that retries transparently retryable exceptions before the application ever sees them - 'With the SDK retrying all transparently retryable exceptions already ... you are only left with terminal exceptions.' This Python page shows the OPPOSITE shape: no built-in RetryStrategy/RetryReason object is named anywhere on the page; instead the application is shown writing and applying its OWN @allow_retries decorator, choosing which exception types to retry and which backoff curve to use, entirely in userland code. Same problem (transient-error retry), structurally different mechanism (SDK-internal orchestration vs. hand-rolled application decorator) - so a Python-specific id is minted rather than forcing reuse.

concepts.label: Durability write ambiguity (TimeoutException / DurabilitySyncWriteAmbiguousException on a single KV write)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a single-operation ambiguity distinct in SCOPE from the promoted sdk:transaction-error-handling, which the registry describes as 'whole-transaction commit ambiguity' documented on a dedicated transactions-error-handling page. This page's ambiguity concerns one durable KV write ('your application requests that a new document be created ... it's ambiguous to the app whether the operation succeeded or not'), not a multi-statement transaction, so it is not the same concept even though both use the word 'ambiguous'/'ambiguity' - no page states the two are the same, so per the no-silent-merge rule they stay apart.

concepts.label: QueryErrorContext / AnalyticsErrorContext (structured error metadata on CouchbaseException)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - REJECTED reuse of sdk:query-error-mapping after checking the page. Java's extraction-layer sdk:query-error-mapping is a many-server-error-code-to-many-typed-exception MAPPING TABLE (PlanningFailureException, IndexFailure, PreparedStatementFailure, keyed by numbered ID ranges). This Python page shows one generic exception type (CouchbaseException) carrying a structured `.context` object (QueryErrorContext, with statement/first_error_code/first_error_message/client_context_id/endpoint fields) rather than a family of distinctly-typed exceptions per error class. Different shape - a single exception with an inspectable context object, not a typed-exception taxonomy - so minting rather than reusing.

notable_absence.finding: No RetryReason-style enum appears anywhere on this page - the retry section is entirely prose-and-decorator, with retry STRATEGIES named only as bullet-point prose ('Retry with an exponentially increasing delay and a delay ceiling', etc.) rather than as a closed, named value set the SDK exposes as an enum. This absence is itself the evidence behind rejecting sdk:retry-strategy/sdk:retry-reason reuse - see cross_product_finding.

cross_component_finding: The page's 'Ambiguity' and 'Non-Idempotent Operations' sections are tightly coupled: idempotency classification (repeated-set vs. counter-increment) is presented as the deciding factor for whether an ambiguous-exception retry is safe to do blindly or needs a read-back first - 'Idempotent operations are much easier to handle, as on ambiguous error results ... the operation can simply be retried' vs. 'After an ambiguous exception on a Non-Idempotent operation, you should first read the document to check for yourself.' This is a real, page-stated coupling between two ideas that would otherwise look independent.
cross_product_finding: This page is the batch's clearest case of correctly REJECTING a suggested reuse rather than forcing it. Three Java-derived extraction-layer ids looked like plausible targets and all three failed the check: (1) sdk:retry-strategy assumes an SDK-built-in, transparent RetryStrategy/RetryReason orchestration layer that simply isn't named anywhere on this Python page - the page instead shows the application hand-rolling its own @allow_retries decorator, a structurally different (userland, not SDK-internal) mechanism, so sdk:custom-retry-decorator was minted instead. (2) sdk:transaction-error-handling is explicitly scoped by the registry to 'whole-transaction commit ambiguity' - this page's ambiguity (TimeoutException / DurabilitySyncWriteAmbiguousException on ONE durable KV write, no transaction involved) is a different scope entirely, so sdk:durability-write-ambiguity was minted rather than reusing the transaction-scoped id despite the shared vocabulary word 'ambiguous'. (3) sdk:query-error-mapping is a many-error-code-to-many-typed-exception table; this page shows one generic exception type carrying a structured .context object instead, so sdk:query-error-context was minted. By contrast, sdk:error-handling, sdk:cas-optimistic-locking and sdk:durability DID reuse cleanly - the base-exception-class design, the CAS-mismatch mechanism, and the ServerDurability option are all genuinely identical mechanisms across the two SDKs. This page is a good stress test of the round's instruction to reject reuse when it doesn't actually hold.
